citations.title: Patient rights
citations.requirement: The governing authority must adopt written patient-rights policies and procedures. Patients get their rights in writing before care starts, with documentation in the clinical record (a)(1). They get a statement of services and charges (a)(2). They are told before care how much third-party payers are expected to pay and how much the patient must pay (a)(3). Any change must be given within 30 calendar days of the agency learning of it, orally and in writing (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Other rights: be told what services will be provided and by whom (a)(4); take part in care planning (a)(5); refuse care (a)(6); complain free of reprisal (a)(7)-(9); be treated with respect (a)(10); privacy of records (a)(11); refuse advanced home health aide tasks (a)(12). Agencies must tell patients they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management (a)(9). All care staff must know these rights (b). A legally authorized representative exercises the rights if the patient lacks capacity (c).

citations.title: Patient service policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Each service needs written policies and procedures, reviewed and revised as necessary (a)(1). Service delivery is documented in the clinical record (a)(2). Continuity: the same personnel serve the same patient where possible (a)(3). Caregivers carry current ID showing name, title, photo and agency name, returned on separation (a)(4). Written procedures cover storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies and equipment (a)(5). Any new nursing or therapeutic service must go to the QI committee first (a)(7). A discharge plan starts before discharge (a)(8). Discharge happens only after notice to the authorized practitioner and consultation with the patient and staff, at least 48 hours before discharge (a)(9). "Health care services" are defined in (b) and include personal care.

citations.title: Plan of care
citations.requirement: A patient is accepted only after an RN, or a person directly supervised by an RN, determines the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs (a). A plan of care is built on a professional assessment (b). It covers diagnosis, prognosis, mental status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential. The plan is reviewed and revised as often as needed, and at least every six months, with each review documented in the clinical record (d)(1). Staff promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition (d)(2).

citations.title: Medical orders
citations.requirement: Section 766.4 exists in Part 766 (title confirmed from the Part 766 table of contents). The text was not retrieved. §766.2(a)(9) refers to 766.4(b) for the definition of "authorized practitioner". Confirm the full text before quoting in the manual.

citations.title: Clinical supervision
citations.requirement: The governing authority must ensure sufficient trained supervisory staff (a). Supervision includes case review, in-home visits to direct and evaluate care, clinical consultation, and consultation on policy. Evidence of adequate supervision (b): services delivered at the planned times and frequencies; assignment by licensure, training and demonstrated skill; prompt charting and reporting of changes in condition, adverse reactions, and problems with informal supports or the home; plans revised as needed. Aides are supervised "as appropriate" by an RN (c). In-home professional supervision occurs (d): (1) at the initial service visit or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience in the tasks, with return demonstration; (2) when a change in condition occurs, to evaluate and revise the plan; (3) to instruct the aide on required observations and written reports. Paragraph (e) covers advanced home health aides (RN home visit at least every two weeks). Not applicable unless the agency uses AHHAs.

citations.title: Patient care record
citations.requirement: Each patient has a confidential record (a) containing: identifying data; medical orders; nursing assessments; the plan of care; signed and dated progress notes after each visit or phone contact; RN supervisory reports; aide observations and activity sheets; documentation of accidents and incidents (a)(8); documentation that rights information was received (a)(9); and a discharge summary (a)(10). Records are kept securely at least 6 years after discharge and are available to DOH (b). For minors, keep until 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer (c). If the agency closes, the governing authority must arrange storage and access and notify DOH in writing where records are kept (d). Written policies must safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access and govern use, removal and release (e).

citations.title: Governing authority
citations.requirement: The governing authority is responsible for operation and compliance with all laws (a)-(b). It must keep a current written emergency plan and orient all employees to it (c). It adopts and amends policies (d) and makes public its services, service area, charges and payment mechanisms (e). It provides an adequate office with access to patient records and prompt phone contact (f). It employs enough staff (g). It employs at least one licensed, registered RN to direct and supervise all patient care (h). It accepts only patients whose needs can be met under written criteria (i). The complaint procedure (j) requires a complaint log; a written response within 15 days; notice of the right to appeal; appeal review by a governing-authority member or committee within 30 days; and notice of the right to complain to DOH. A continuous QI program is required (k). A QI committee with a consumer and health professionals meets at least four times a year (l): it reviews policies; reviews a random sample of current patients' and past-3-month discharges' records plus all complaint cases; and sends a written summary to the governing authority. Management contracts (m) and franchise agreements (n) need prior written commissioner consent; submit proposals at least 60 days before the effective date. Subdivision (o): HPN accounts, 24/7 emergency contacts, a written HPN coverage policy reviewed at least annually, and directory updates at least monthly.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: The agency may contract for patient care services. Services by arrangement require a written contract (b). Contract personnel must meet §766.11 personnel requirements (c). The agency remains responsible for the adequacy of contracted services (d). Nurses or therapists under contract must coordinate and integrate with agency services (e). Subdivision (f) addresses personal care contracts with local social services districts. Only the opening text of this section was seen; confirm the full text.

citations.title: Personnel
citations.requirement: Written personnel policies are reviewed at least annually (a). Aide qualifications under §700.2 must be met, and the PHL §3613(3)(a)-(f) information must be in the Home Care Registry (b). Health status is assessed before assuming duties (c). For personnel with direct patient contact (d): rubella immunity; measles immunity if born on or after 1/1/1957; TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test before employment and annually; an annual health status assessment; and influenza vaccination documentation or a mask during flu season. Identity is verified before hire (e). Employment history and references are verified before patient contact, and a criminal history record check is run as required by Part 402 (f). Personnel records hold verifications, licenses, evaluations and employment dates; health records are kept separate and confidential (g). Time and payment records are kept (h). Orientation is required, and in-service is at least 12 hours a year for HHAs, 6 for PCAs and 18 for AHHAs (i). Each position has a written job description (j). An annual performance assessment includes at least one in-home observation visit where applicable (k). A bloodborne-pathogen program (l) covers barriers, training at hire and yearly, PPE, monitoring, and an exposure-management procedure.

citations.title: Records and reports
citations.requirement: The agency must promptly submit all records and reports DOH requires (a). The principal NYS office keeps: the license, organizational documents, assumed-name certificate, patient-care contracts, governing-authority and QA bylaws, current policies, a current patient roster and a listing of all personnel (a)(1). Branch offices keep policies, a personnel list and patient records (a)(2). Retention minimums (a)(3): governing authority and committee minutes, 3 years; patient-care financial records, 3 years; personnel records, 3 years after separation; complaint and grievance records, 3 years after resolution; patient care records per §766.6. Electronic records must be secure, confidential and printable on request (b). Each year the agency furnishes DOH with statistical summaries of services and reimbursement, plus an ownership list (c).

citations.title: Definitions (home care services agency; licensed home care services agency; aide qualifications)
citations.requirement: Defines a home care services agency (a)(6) and a licensed home care services agency (a)(25) as one licensed under PHL Article 36. Per the fact-checked research, it also defines personal care aide and home health aide qualifications and training. The aide-definition text was past the truncation point in the fetch.

citations.title: Medicaid personal care services: scope, levels, minimum needs, assessment and authorization
citations.requirement: Personal care must be medically necessary, ordered by a qualified independent practitioner, based on assessment, delivered under a plan of care and supervised by an RN (a)(1). Eligibility requires a stable medical condition and self-direction, with the exceptions stated (a)(3)(i)-(ii). Minimum needs (a)(3)(iv): dementia or Alzheimer's needs supervision with more than one ADL; all others need limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs. Continuous PCS is more than 16 hours/day by more than one aide (a)(2). Live-in 24-hour PCS is one aide whose sleep is likely to be uninterrupted for 5 hours (a)(4). Level I covers nutritional and environmental support tasks only, authorized for no more than 8 hours/week (a)(5)(i). Level II adds personal care functions (a)(5)(ii)(a)(1)-(13), including medication prompting and assistance, but not administration (a)(5)(ii)(a)(10). Additional documentation is needed before authorizing more than 12 hours/day on average (a)(5)(ii)(b). Assessment (b): an independent RN assessment (RN licensed in NYS with 2+ years of home care experience), an independent medical exam and practitioner order, and plan development by the district or MMCO. Telehealth is allowed if an in-person option is offered.

citations.title: Personal care aide training and qualifications
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: a personal care aide for Medicaid needs a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training, completed within 3 months of hire, plus 3 hours of in-service semiannually. Subdivision (e) text was not seen in the truncated fetch.

citations.title: Nursing supervision of personal care aides
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: an RN supervisory visit at least every 90 days, with a combined visit possible every six months for stable, self-directing clients. Later DOH rulemaking amended (f)(3)(vi) so the local district or MMCO determines the supervision frequency (regs.health.ny.gov summary of express terms). OMIG audit guidance says some counties require only six-month visits, so the frequency must be stated on the plan of care or in the contract. Keep a written report for each visit with the aide present. Confirm the current (f) text and the MLTC contract.

citations.title: Criminal history record check process
citations.requirement: Request a check for each prospective employee (a). An authorized person signs the DOH form, and the form and two sets of fingerprints go to DOH within 10 business days (excluding weekends and legal holidays) of taking the prints (b). The applicant presents two IDs, one government-issued with signature and at least one with photo (c)(1). Resubmit within 14 days of notice that prints were rejected (c)(3). Temporary approval is allowed pending results, with the §402.4 supervision (d). An expedited review request applies if the person has a prior determination or a pending submission (e).

citations.title: Home Care Worker Registry
citations.requirement: Part 403 applies to every Article 36 licensed agency. The agency must designate at least two individuals to access and enter data in the registry (§403.3(a)), and it must have policies implementing Part 403 (§403.3(b)). Only designated individuals may submit data (§403.3(c)). Within 10 business days after an aide begins providing services, the registry must be updated with employment information including the start date (§403.5(a)(6), as described in DOH DAL 19-21). A person trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted to the registry (§403.5).

citations.title: Home care services workers (registry)
citations.requirement: Establishes the Home Care Services Worker Registry and the information entered for each worker who completes a state-approved training program (name, address, gender, date of birth, program). Also provides for indicating advanced home health aide status and any limitation or revocation of that status.

citations.title: Licensure of home care services agencies
citations.requirement: A license is required to provide nursing, home health aide or personal care services. PHHPC approval considers public need, character and competence, and financial resources. The application fee is $2,000 (subd. 13), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Annual LHCSA registration
citations.requirement: Annual registration since 1/1/2019. Unregistered agencies may not operate or be paid. The late penalty is $500 per month, and missing two registration periods can lead to revocation.

citations.title: Home care worker wage parity
citations.requirement: For Medicaid-funded home care in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester: total compensation is the home care aide minimum plus a benefit portion of $2.54/hour (NYC) or $1.67/hour (Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester) from 1/1/2024. Requires an annual certification and an independently audited statement. Records are kept 10 years, per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Home care aide minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage for home care aides: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of state) as of 1/1/2026. This rises to $20.00 and $19.00 on 1/1/2027.

citations.title: Cost reporting
citations.requirement: Cost reports are filed when DOH requires them: within 90 days of notice, with a 30-day correction window (2018 amendments), per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Application review standards; determinations of public need
citations.requirement: Character, competence and financial feasibility standards, with working capital of at least two months of estimated operating expenses (§765-1.2). Public need rebuttable presumption of no need where 5 or more LHCSAs each actively serve 25+ patients in a county. Initial applicants must commit to serve hard-to-reach groups (§765-1.16(e)). Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Influenza vaccination or mask for health care personnel
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced from §766.11(d)(6). The section text itself was not fetched. Confirm the current rule text before quoting in the manual.

citations.title: HIV/bloodborne pathogen definitions and exposure standards
citations.requirement: Cross-referenced from §766.11(l)(1) for the definition of significant-risk body substances. The section text itself was not fetched. Confirm before quoting.

citations.title: Medicaid provider compliance programs
citations.requirement: Medicaid providers that meet the statutory billing threshold must keep an effective compliance program. NOT retrieved or verified here; confirm applicability and the threshold with counsel or OMIG before adopting. The compliance policy should be written either way.

citations.cite: DOH MLTC Policy: LHCSA contract limits
citations.title: Licensed Home Care Services Agencies contract guidance
citations.requirement: MLTC plans may contract with no more than 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state, with at least two LHCSAs per county accepting new enrollees. Exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: DOH Electronic Visit Verification (21st Century Cures Act, 42 USC 1396b(l))
citations.title: EVV for Medicaid personal care
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services from 1/1/2021 (choice model: the agency picks its own vendor), with data sent to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator. It captures date, location, service, people, and start and end times. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Minimum Needs Requirements effective 9/1/2025
citations.requirement: Adults 21+ seeking PCS or CDPAS must need limited assistance with more than two ADLs (more than one ADL with supervision for dementia or Alzheimer's). It applies to initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025, and to Medicaid recipients 18+ seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.title: Weekly HERDS reporting by LHCSAs
citations.requirement: Weekly HERDS reporting includes patient census by licensed county. The window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m. (since 6/17/2025). Contact hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov. Per the fact-checked research.

citations.cite: NYSDOH LHCSA Policy & Procedure Manual Review Tool (Part B)
citations.title: DOH review tool for LHCSA P&P manuals
citations.requirement: DOH reviewers check P&P manuals against 10 NYCRR 766 (including §766.11(b)-(c)) and Part 403 registry provisions. Use it as the surveyor's checklist.

citations.title: PCA/HHA/AHHA training documentation verification
citations.requirement: When hiring aides, review the available training materials to confirm training from a DOH- or SED-approved program. The materials must include the Home Care Registry aide profile; the training certificate is included if available.

citations.cite: OMIG Audit Protocol: Personal Care Aides (guidance, rev. 5/11/15)
citations.title: Personal care audit criteria
citations.requirement: Audit guidance only; it does not create legal requirements. It describes disallowance of claims where there is no documented RN supervisory visit within 120 days before the sampled date of service. A written report is needed for each visit. The visit frequency should appear on the plan of care or in the contract.

citations.cite: DOH Medicaid Managed Care NYIA guidance
citations.title: MMC guidance on NYIA, plan of care and authorizations
citations.requirement: The plan remains responsible for authorizing services and must record the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services in the plan of care, with notice to the enrollee. Plans coordinate with the NYIA on assessments and practitioner orders (18 NYCRR 505.14(b)(2)(iii)).

citations.title: P&P manual and pre-opening survey
citations.requirement: After PHHPC contingent approval, the P&P manual goes to the regional home care office. The regional office must accept it before the pre-opening survey. Per the fact-checked research.

policies.title: Governing Authority, Operator and RN Director of Patient Services Responsibilities
state_specifics: The governing authority (operator) manages the agency and ensures compliance with all federal, state and local law, §766.9(a)-(b).

It must employ at least one licensed, currently registered RN responsible for directing and supervising all patient care, §766.9(h). The RN's qualifications are set by the agency for the duties assigned.
It must employ or contract for enough staff, and keep an office with access to records and prompt phone contact, §766.9(f)-(g).
Part 766 sets no administrator credential. At least one principal must show health care experience per the application.
Policies are adopted and amended by the governing authority, §766.9(d), and a surveyor will review this manual.

policies.title: Licensure, Counties Served, Annual Registration and Public Information
state_specifics: Serve only in counties named on the license. Adding a county, service or site needs an administrative amendment: regional office or homecareapplications@health.ny.gov. New counties remain subject to the public-need rule.
Annual registration under PHL §3605-b: $500 per month late penalty, and missing two periods can lead to revocation.
Make public the services, geographic area, charges and payment mechanisms, §766.9(e).
Keep the license, organizational documents and a current patient roster and personnel list at the principal NYS office, §766.12(a)(1).
The license is not transferable. A change of ownership needs a new CON application.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Personnel policies are reviewed at least annually and revised as necessary, §766.11(a).
Service policies are reviewed and revised as necessary, §766.2(a)(1).
The HPN coverage policy is reviewed at least annually, §766.9(o).
The QI committee reviews service policies and recommends changes; the governing authority adopts them, §766.9(l)(1).
Keep the current policy set at the principal office and every branch, §766.12(a)(1)(vii), (a)(2)(i). Keep governing-authority and committee minutes 3 years, §766.12(a)(3)(i).

policies.title: Quality Improvement Program and QI Committee
state_specifics: QI committee: a consumer plus appropriate health professionals, meeting at least four times a year, §766.9(l).
Each meeting reviews policies and a clinical record review. Records are randomly selected from current patients and patients discharged in the past 3 months, plus all cases with patient complaints.
A written summary of findings goes to the governing authority for action. Keep minutes 3 years.
Quality is every staff member's responsibility at all times, §766.9(k).
Any service the agency has not previously provided in homes goes to the QI committee before routine provision, §766.2(a)(7).

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: The practitioner order is subject to 18 NYCRR Parts 515-518 (OMIG sanctions and overpayment recovery), §505.14(b)(2)(ii)(i).
Bill only authorized services actually delivered. Support claims with EVV data, timesheets and documented RN supervisory visits.
Keep patient-care financial records 3 years, §766.12(a)(3)(ii). Keep wage parity records 10 years.
Whether Part 521 requires a formal compliance program for your billing volume is unverified; confirm with counsel or OMIG. Adopt a written compliance program regardless.
Management or franchise arrangements cannot transfer control of billing or books and records, §766.9(m)-(n).

policies.title: Management Contracts, Franchise Agreements and Contracted Services
state_specifics: A management contract or franchise agreement takes effect only with prior written consent of the commissioner. Submit the proposal at least 60 days before the effective date, §766.9(m)(4), (n)(2).
The governing authority must keep control of hire/fire of the administrator, books and records, assets and liabilities, and independent adoption of policies, §766.9(m)(2)(iii), (n)(3).
Terminating a management contract for cause: not more than 60 days' notice, with written notice to DOH and a continuation plan, §766.9(m)(6).
Services by arrangement require a written contract. Contract personnel must meet §766.11 requirements. The agency remains responsible for service adequacy, §766.10(b)-(d).
Nurses or therapists under contract coordinate with agency care planning and supervision, §766.10(e).

policies.title: Health Provider Network (HPN) Accounts, 24/7 Emergency Contacts and Coverage
state_specifics: Obtain HPN accounts and keep them current, with designated HPN coordinator(s) and enough staff users for rapid response to DOH requests, §766.9(o)(1)-(2).
List 24-hour, seven-day-a-week emergency contacts in the HPN communications directory, §766.9(o).
Update the directory when personnel roles change and at least monthly, §766.9(o)(4).
Maintain a written HPN coverage policy consistent with hours of operation and review it at least annually.
Weekly HERDS census submission: window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m.; contact hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov.

policies.title: Patient Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Give rights in writing before care starts and document it in the clinical record, §766.1(a)(1); §766.6(a)(9).
Rights are listed at §766.1(a)(1)-(12): service information, care-plan participation, refusal, complaints without reprisal, dignity, privacy.
All staff providing care must know the rights and promote them, §766.1(b). A legal representative exercises rights for patients lacking capacity, §766.1(c).
Medicaid MLTC members also have fair hearing and plan appeal rights under their plan's notices. Provide those notices when authorization changes occur.

policies.title: Patient Complaints and Appeals
state_specifics: Keep a complaint log with dates received and resolved, §766.9(j)(1).
Written response to every written complaint (and oral complaints if requested), explaining findings and decisions to date, within 15 days of receipt, §766.9(j)(2)(i).
Advise the complainant of the right to appeal. The appeal is reviewed by a member or committee of the governing authority within 30 days of receipt, §766.9(j)(3).

Notify the patient or designee that they may complain to the DOH Office of Health Systems Management, §766.1(a)(9); §766.9(j)(4). DOH home care complaint hotline number: confirm the current number before printing in the manual (not verified here).
Complaints include lack of respect for property by anyone serving on the agency's behalf, §766.1(a)(9). Complaints are free from interference, coercion, discrimination or reprisal, §766.1(a)(8).
Complaint cases are reviewed by the QI committee, §766.9(l)(2)(ii). Retain complaint records 3 years from resolution, §766.12(a)(3)(iv).

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Patients may refuse release of records to anyone outside the agency, except on transfer to a health care facility, as required by law, or under a third-party payment contract, §766.1(a)(11).
Written policies must safeguard records against loss or unauthorized access and govern use, removal and release, §766.6(e).
Electronic records must be secure from unwarranted access and printable on request for the agency and DOH, §766.12(b).
Employee health records are kept apart from the personnel file and treated with the same confidentiality as patient records, §766.11(g).
Criminal history results may be used solely for authorized purposes under Exec. Law §845-b and PHL art. 28-E, §402.6(b)(3)-(4).

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Complaints about disrespect for the patient's property are covered by the complaint procedure, §766.1(a)(9); §766.9(j).
Patients must be treated with respect and recognition of dignity and individuality, §766.1(a)(10).
Level I tasks include shopping, payment of bills and essential errands, §505.14(a)(5)(i)(a)(6),(8). Require receipts and a documented record of any client funds handled.
Document accidents and incidents, including alleged theft, in the patient record, §766.6(a)(8).
Gift, loan and money-handling rules are agency-adopted standards. No specific Part 766 section on gifts was located.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Patients have the right to be treated with consideration, respect and full recognition of dignity and individuality, §766.1(a)(10).
Provide rights information orally and in writing, including payment information, §766.1(a)(3)(ii). Offer it in the patient's language.
Under 18 NYCRR 505.14(b)(2)(iii)(a)(3), the district or MMCO must consider the individual's preferences and social and cultural considerations in care planning.
Every initial LHCSA applicant must commit to serve people who have trouble getting care because of minority status, age, case complexity, payment source or location, §765-1.16(e).

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Before care starts, give a statement of available services and related charges, §766.1(a)(2).
Before care starts, explain the extent to which payment is expected from third-party payers and the extent the patient may have to pay, orally and in writing, §766.1(a)(3), (a)(3)(ii).
Report any change in this information within 30 calendar days of learning of it, §766.1(a)(3)(i).
Make charges and payment mechanisms available to the public, §766.9(e).
Medicaid/MLTC patients: do not charge for services the plan authorizes. Document the plan's authorization (level, amount, frequency, duration) in the service agreement.

policies.title: Scope of Services: What Personal Care Aides May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Level I (nutritional and environmental support only), §505.14(a)(5)(i)(a): making/changing beds; dusting and vacuuming rooms the patient uses; light cleaning of kitchen, bedroom and bathroom; dishwashing; listing needed supplies; shopping if no other arrangements; laundry including ironing and mending; bill payment and essential errands; meal preparation including simple modified diets.

Level II adds personal care functions, §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a): bathing; dressing; grooming; toileting; walking; transferring; turning and positioning; modified-diet meals (low sugar, fat, salt, residue); feeding; patient self-administration support; routine skin care; use of medical equipment (walkers, wheelchairs); changing simple dressings.
Supervision and cueing are not standalone services, §505.14(a)(5)(iii).
Advanced home health aide tasks are not offered unless the license and RN supervision under §766.5(e) are in place. Patients may refuse AHHA tasks, in which case an RN does them, §766.1(a)(12).
Any nursing or therapeutic procedure new to the agency requires QI committee review first, §766.2(a)(7).
Level I authorization may not exceed 8 hours per week, §505.14(a)(5)(i)(b).

policies.title: Patient Intake, Acceptance Criteria and RN Determination
state_specifics: Accept and retain only patients whose needs can be safely met, per written criteria, §766.9(i).
An RN, or an individual directly supervised by an RN, must determine before acceptance that the agency can safely and adequately meet the patient's needs, §766.3(a).
Medicaid personal care requires a stable medical condition and self-direction, unless the §505.14(a)(3)(ii) exceptions are met (a responsible person assumes decision-making).
Medicaid personal care requires meeting the minimum needs requirements (see SVC-04). If a referral does not meet them, decline and refer back to the plan.
Document the rights notice and charge disclosure before the first visit (see CR-01, CR-06).

policies.title: Medicaid Independent Assessment, Practitioner Order and Reassessment
state_specifics: Initial independent assessment by a DOH-designated entity, performed by a NYS RN with at least 2 years of recent home health care experience, §505.14(b)(2)(i).
Independent medical exam and practitioner order (physician, PA, specialist assistant or NP). The examiner must be independent, with no prior provider-patient relationship, §505.14(b)(2)(ii).
The district or MMCO (the plan) reviews the assessment and order, then authorizes services and develops the plan of care, §505.14(b)(2)(iii).
Plans record the level, amount, frequency and duration of authorized services and send notice to the enrollee (DOH MMC guidance).

Routine reassessments are annual per DOH's response in the rulemaking. Authorizations should not exceed 12 months (fact-checked research). Do not start or continue services without a current authorization from the plan.

policies.title: Minimum Needs Requirements and Level I/Level II Authorization Limits
state_specifics: Minimum needs, §505.14(a)(3)(iv): for diagnosed dementia or Alzheimer's, at least supervision with more than one ADL; all others, at least limited assistance with physical maneuvering with more than two ADLs.
Applies to PCS/CDPAS applicants 21+ and to Medicaid recipients 18+ seeking MLTC or MAP enrollment, at initial assessments and reassessments on or after 9/1/2025 (DOH page).
Level I: no more than 8 hours/week, §505.14(a)(5)(i)(b).
More than 12 hours/day on average (including continuous and live-in) requires added plan documentation, §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(b) and (b)(2)(v).
Do not schedule beyond the plan's authorization. Refer reauthorization questions to the care manager.

policies.title: Live-in 24-Hour and Continuous Personal Care Services
state_specifics: Continuous PCS: uninterrupted care by more than one aide for more than 16 hours in a calendar day, for patients with frequent need (toileting, walking, transferring, turning/positioning or feeding) such that a live-in aide would be unlikely to get 5 hours of uninterrupted sleep, §505.14(a)(2).
Live-in 24-hour PCS: one aide, for patients whose need is sufficiently infrequent that the aide would likely get 5 hours of uninterrupted sleep in an 8-hour sleep period, §505.14(a)(4).
The patient's home must have sleeping accommodations for the live-in aide (see the amended §505.14(b)(2)(v) text).
Staff live-in aides to meet minimum wage and wage parity rules; see PER-06 and PER-11.

policies.title: Plan of Care and Plan Updates
state_specifics: The plan is built on a professional assessment and lists diagnosis, prognosis, mental status, frequency of each service, medications, treatments, diet regimens, functional limitations and rehabilitation potential, §766.3(b).
Review and revise as often as needed, and at least every 6 months, documenting each review, §766.3(d)(1).
Promptly alert the authorized practitioner and other affected providers to significant changes in condition, §766.3(d)(2). Report plan changes to the payer authorizing services, §766.5(b)(4).
Patients take part in planning and are advised in advance of plan changes, §766.1(a)(5).
The plan sits in the patient record, §766.6(a)(4).

policies.title: Supervision of Aides and RN Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: Aides are supervised "as appropriate" by an RN, §766.5(c). Professional in-home supervision takes place at the initial service visit, or on a change in personnel, if the aide lacks documented training and experience for the tasks, §766.5(d)(1).
Supervise in the home when the patient's condition changes, to evaluate and revise the plan, §766.5(d)(2). Instruct aides on what to observe and report, §766.5(d)(3).

Medicaid supervisory visits: the traditional frequency is every 90 days. OMIG audit guidance notes some counties require every six months, particularly for Level I; later DOH rulemaking leaves frequency to the district or MMCO, §505.14(f)(3)(vi). State the frequency on the plan of care and confirm in each MLTC contract.
Only an RN may make the visit, and the aide should be present. Write a report for each visit and file it in the record, §766.6(a)(6). OMIG disallows claims without documentation.
Annual performance assessment of every aide includes at least one in-home observation, §766.11(k).

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Personal care aides may support the patient's own administration of medication, §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a)(10): prompting the patient as to time; identifying the medication; bringing the medication and supplies; opening the container; positioning the patient; disposing of used supplies; storing the medication properly.

Aides do not administer medication. Medication administration by an advanced home health aide requires an RN comprehensive medication review and direct RN supervision, §766.5(e)(v), and is outside this manual unless the agency adds AHHA services.
Aides report medication problems to the supervising RN and record them in observation notes, §766.6(a)(7).

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: To the extent possible, the same personnel serve the same patient, §766.2(a)(3).
Supervision is adequate when staff provide services at the times and frequencies in the plan of care, §766.5(b)(1). Document missed visits and make-up or backup coverage.
Staff are assigned according to licensure, training, orientation and demonstrated skills, §766.5(b)(2).
The emergency plan must keep patient health needs met during disruptions, §766.9(c). Maintain 24/7 contacts, §766.9(o).
Notify the plan or care manager when authorized hours are not delivered.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid personal care since 1/1/2021 (choice model: the agency chooses its vendor). Data goes to the NYS EVV Data Aggregator.
EVV captures date, location, service type, people, and start and end times.
Time and payment records are kept for all personnel, §766.11(h).
Reconcile EVV against authorizations before billing. Keep an EVV exceptions log.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Changes in condition, adverse reactions and problems with informal supports or the home must be charted promptly and reported to supervisory staff, §766.5(b)(3).
An RN evaluates in the home and initiates plan revisions, §766.5(d)(2). Promptly alert the authorized practitioner, §766.3(d)(2).
Document accidents and incidents, §766.6(a)(8).
Aides call 911 for life-threatening emergencies, then notify the RN. This is agency procedure rather than a named Part 766 rule.

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Start a discharge plan before discharge, §766.2(a)(8).
Discharge only after notifying the authorized practitioner and consulting the patient and professional staff involved in the plan of care, at least 48 hours before discharge, §766.2(a)(9).
The discharge summary includes planning, notice to the practitioner, reasons and date, summary of care, status at discharge, remaining needs, self-management ability and referrals, §766.6(a)(10).
For MLTC members, coordinate with the plan, which holds the authorization and member notice responsibilities.

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs, MLTC Plans and Payers
state_specifics: Medicaid personal care is authorized by the local district or MMCO. The plan must record level, amount, frequency and duration, §505.14(b)(2)(iii); DOH MMC guidance.
Plans may contract with 1 LHCSA per 100 enrollees downstate or per 60 rest of state, with at least two LHCSAs per county accepting new enrollees. Contract exceptions: LHCSAExceptions@health.ny.gov.
Get the rate, billing codes and units, authorization process and wage pass-through in writing in each MLTC contract.
CDPAP: PPL is the Statewide Fiscal Intermediary and LHCSAs no longer serve as CDPAP FIs. Refer patients who want CDPAP to the plan or care manager.
The district or MMCO decides whether CDPAP, personal emergency response, shared aide or other services are more appropriate, §505.14(b)(2)(iii)(a).

policies.title: Introduction of New Services and Procedures (QI Committee Review)
state_specifics: Any nursing or therapeutic service, procedure or treatment not previously provided in homes by the agency is first reviewed by the QI committee, §766.2(a)(7).
If a patient needs it urgently, it may be implemented before QI review if medical consultation on safety and appropriateness was obtained and staff are trained for that specific service.
Adding services or counties to the license is a separate DOH amendment (see GOV-02).

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: No section of Part 766 was located that prescribes an abuse-reporting procedure or deadline for LHCSAs. The policy is agency-adopted under §766.9(b), (d).
Pre-hire protections: a criminal history record check (§402.6), Home Care Registry check and reference verification (§766.11(f)).
Patients may complain without reprisal and are told how to reach DOH, §766.1(a)(8)-(9).
Document allegations and incidents in the record, §766.6(a)(8).
Before finalizing, have counsel confirm any NY mandated-reporter duties and the Adult Protective Services referral process. These were not verified here.

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Document accidents and incidents in the patient record, §766.6(a)(8). Report changes in condition and problems to supervisory staff, §766.5(b)(3).
Review incident patterns through the QI committee, §766.9(l).
Use the 24/7 HPN contacts for DOH alerts, §766.9(o).
No Part 766 deadline for reporting incidents to DOH was located. Set an agency timeline (e.g., supervisor notice the same day) and confirm any MLTC contract reporting rules.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Written procedures for storage, cleaning and disinfection of supplies, equipment and appliances, §766.2(a)(5).
Staff TB assessment and test before employment and annually; written policy on follow-up of positive results, §766.11(d)(4).
Annual influenza vaccination documentation, or a surgical or procedure mask during flu season for those not vaccinated, §766.11(d)(6) (cross-reference to 10 NYCRR §2.59).
Measles and rubella immunity records, §766.11(d)(1)-(2). Medical exemption statements are kept in the personnel record, §766.11(d)(3).

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Plan for each patient's continued care during emergencies that interfere with service delivery, §766.9(c).
RN identifies patients with high need for uninterrupted care. Document the emergency contact and plan for each patient in the record.
Staff are oriented to their responsibilities in the emergency plan, §766.9(c).
Use HPN alerts and 24/7 contacts to receive DOH emergency communications, §766.9(o).

policies.title: Agency Emergency Plan and Continuity of Operations
state_specifics: Keep a current written emergency plan with procedures to ensure patients' health care needs continue to be met in emergencies that interfere with service delivery, §766.9(c).
Orient all employees to the plan, §766.9(c).
Keep records and the office accessible so professional staff can reach patient records, §766.9(f); back up electronic records securely, §766.12(b).
If the agency closes, arrange for records and notify DOH in writing where they are stored, §766.6(d).

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Supervisory staff review problems with the home environment and informal supports, §766.5(b)(3).
PPE appropriate to tasks is provided, §766.11(l)(1)(iv).
No Part 766 section on workplace violence was located. Adopt an agency policy for unsafe homes, aggression and the right to leave and report.

policies.title: Bloodborne Pathogen and Significant-Risk Body Substance Exposure Program
state_specifics: Program required by §766.11(l): protective barriers, safe practices with contaminated equipment, training at hire and yearly, PPE, and monitoring.

Exposure management procedure: report to a designated person; evaluate and follow up the exposure, including source assessment, counseling and voluntary testing, and medical follow-up for the exposed person, §766.11(l)(2).
Disclosure of source HIV status needs express written consent or court order. Keep exposure reports confidential, §766.11(l)(2)(ii)(b), (iii).

policies.title: Errands, Escort and Client Transportation
state_specifics: Level I includes shopping if no other arrangements are possible and essential errands, §505.14(a)(5)(i)(a)(6),(8). Level II includes walking within and outside the home, §505.14(a)(5)(ii)(a)(5).
No Part 766 rule on driving patients was located. If aides drive, the agency sets vehicle, insurance, license and mileage-reimbursement standards (agency policy).
Escort and errands are performed only as listed in the authorized plan of care.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Training Credentials and Certification
state_specifics: Aides must meet the §700.2 qualifications, §766.11(b)(1).
Medicaid personal care aides need a DOH-approved HHA program or the 40-hour PCA basic training, completed within 3 months of hire and before service per the research checklist, §505.14(e).
Before assigning, review the training source and the Home Care Registry aide profile (DAL DHCBS 20-05).
HHAs need an approved basic program or equivalency exam. A written job description with education and experience is required for each position, §766.11(j).
Staff are assigned by licensure, training and demonstrated skills, §766.5(b)(2).

policies.title: Background Checks, Identity and Reference Verification
state_specifics: Request a criminal history record check for each prospective employee, §402.6(a); §766.11(f)(2).
An authorized person signs the DOH form and sends it with two sets of fingerprints within 10 business days of taking the prints, §402.6(b).
The applicant shows two forms of ID, one government-issued with signature, and at least one with photo, §402.6(c)(1).
Resubmit within 14 days of notice of rejected prints, §402.6(c)(3). Temporary approval pending results needs the §402.4 supervision, §402.6(d).

Verify identity before retention, §766.11(e). Before patient contact, verify employment history and references (or recommendations from unrelated persons for those not previously employed), §766.11(f)(1).
Check the Home Care Registry for the aide's profile. Screen against the OMIG exclusion list (agency practice).

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual In-Service Training
state_specifics: All personnel receive orientation to agency policies and procedures, plus in-service education, §766.11(i).
Minimum in-service per year: HHAs 12 hours, PCAs 6 hours, AHHAs 18 hours (with medication management, infection control and injection safety), §766.11(i)(1)-(3).
Medicaid personal care adds 3 hours semiannually, §505.14(e) (per the research).
Bloodborne pathogen training at hire and yearly, §766.11(l)(1)(iii).
RN demonstrates tasks and gets return demonstration at the initial visit if the aide lacks documented training for them, §766.5(d)(1).

policies.title: Employee Health, Immunization and TB Screening
state_specifics: Health status assessed and documented before patient care duties. No one assumes duties with a health impairment that is a risk to patients or interferes with duties, including habituation or addiction to drugs or alcohol that may alter behavior, §766.11(c).
Rubella certificate; measles immunity (born on or after 1/1/1957); medical exemption statement if applicable, §766.11(d)(1)-(3).

TB: initial individual risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test (skin test or FDA-approved blood assay) before employment, then annual assessments including education and risk assessment. Written follow-up policy for positive results, §766.11(d)(4).
Annual health status assessment, §766.11(d)(5).
Influenza vaccination or mask during influenza season, §766.11(d)(6).
Health records are kept apart from the personnel file and confidential, §766.11(g).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Content: verification of employment history and qualifications, signed and dated application, licenses and registrations, health and physical records (kept separate), performance evaluations, dates of employment and separation, §766.11(g).
Time and payment records, §766.11(h).
Retain personnel records 3 years from termination or resignation, §766.12(a)(3)(iii).
Keep a current listing of all personnel at the principal office and each branch, §766.12(a)(1)(ix), (a)(2)(ii).

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Home care aide minimum wage (PHL §3614-f): $19.65 NYC/Long Island/Westchester and $18.65 rest of state from 1/1/2026; $20.00 and $19.00 from 1/1/2027.
The general NY minimum wage is lower ($17.00/$16.00), but home care aides must be paid the PHL §3614-f minimum (NY DOL).
Keep time and payment records for all personnel, §766.11(h).
Overtime and live-in aide pay rules (federal FLSA, 29 CFR 552) apply. State-specific 24-hour/13-hour rules were not verified here; confirm with counsel.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: All staff must be aware of patient rights and protect and promote them, §766.1(b).
Patients are treated with consideration, respect and full recognition of dignity and individuality, §766.1(a)(10).
Keep records confidential and release them only as policy allows, §766.6(e).
Annual performance assessment covers conduct, §766.11(k).
Staff conduct standards (gifts, social media, personal relationships) are agency-adopted.

policies.title: Caregiver Photo Identification and Badges
state_specifics: Caregivers in homes display proper and current identification with name, title, current photograph and the name of the agency, §766.2(a)(4).
The ID is returned to the agency on termination of employment, §766.2(a)(4).
Replace expired or altered ID promptly. Keep an ID issue and return log.

policies.title: Home Care Worker Registry Entry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Ensure the PHL §3613(3)(a)-(f) information is in the registry, §766.11(b)(2).
Designate at least two staff to access and enter registry data and give DOH their names and contact information, §403.3(a).
Update the registry with employment information including start date within 10 business days after the aide begins services, §403.5(a)(6) (as cited in DAL 19-21).
Aides trained in a state-approved program on or after 9/25/2009 may not provide services until posted in the registry, §403.5.
Keep a written Part 403 policy, §403.3(b). Check the registry aide profile at hire (DAL DHCBS 20-05).

policies.title: Job Descriptions and Annual Performance Evaluation
state_specifics: Current written job description for each position stating responsibilities and education/experience requirements, §766.11(j).
Annual assessment of the performance and effectiveness of all personnel, including at least one in-home visit to observe performance where applicable, §766.11(k).
Keep evaluations in the personnel record, §766.11(g).

policies.title: Home Care Aide Minimum Wage and Wage Parity (Downstate Medicaid)
state_specifics: Home care aide minimum wage, PHL §3614-f: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) / $18.65 (rest of state) in 2026; $20.00 / $19.00 from 1/1/2027. It applies to all payers.

Wage parity, PHL §3614-c: for Medicaid work in NYC, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, add a benefit portion of $2.54 (NYC) or $1.67 (Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester). Total compensation in 2026: $22.19 (NYC) / $21.32 (Nassau/Suffolk/Westchester).
File an annual certification with an independently audited statement. Keep records 10 years.
Check each January whether MLTC contracts pass the wage increase through.

policies.title: Patient Records and Retention
state_specifics: Contents, §766.6(a): identifying data; medical orders; nursing assessments; plan of care; signed and dated progress notes after each visit or phone contact; RN supervisory reports; aide observations and activity sheets; accident/incident documentation; rights-receipt documentation; discharge summary.
Retain at least 6 years after discharge, kept securely and available to DOH, §766.6(b). For minors: 6 years after discharge or 3 years after age 18, whichever is longer, §766.6(c).
If the agency closes, make effective storage and access arrangements and notify DOH in writing, §766.6(d).
Written policies safeguard records and govern use, removal and release, §766.6(e). Electronic records must be secure and printable, §766.12(b).

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual statistical summaries of services and reimbursement on DOH forms; annual ownership list (for-profit stockholders; not-for-profit directors/officers), §766.12(c).
Annual registration (PHL §3605-b). Cost reports when DOH requires them (PHL §3612), within 90 days of notice with a 30-day correction window.
Weekly HERDS survey with patient census by licensed county: window opens Tuesday 8:00 a.m. and closes Thursday 2:00 p.m.; hcstatrpts@health.ny.gov.
Wage parity annual certification and audited statement (PHL §3614-c).
Management contract or franchise proposals to DOH 60 days before effective date, §766.9(m)-(n).
Failure by a supervising RN to meet the AHHA supervision rules must be reported to DOH, §766.5(g) (only if AHHAs are used).

policies.title: Agency Records on File, Branch Offices and Retention Schedule
state_specifics: At the principal NYS office: license; certificate of incorporation or partnership agreement; assumed-name certificate; patient-care contracts; governing-authority and QA bylaws; current operating policies; current patient roster; list of all personnel, §766.12(a)(1).
At each branch: policies, personnel list and the patient roster with patient records, §766.12(a)(2).

Minimum retention: governing-authority and committee minutes 3 years from meeting; patient-care financial records 3 years; personnel records 3 years from separation; complaint records 3 years from resolution; patient care records per §766.6, §766.12(a)(3).
Hard copy or electronic. Electronic records must be secure, confidential and immediately available as hard copy to the agency and DOH, §766.12(b).

forms.name: Patient Rights Notice and Acknowledgment
forms.purpose: Written rights given before care begins, signed and filed in the record; includes DOH complaint contact.

forms.name: Statement of Services, Charges and Payer Disclosure
forms.purpose: Available services, charges, expected third-party payment and patient liability, given orally and in writing; change notice within 30 days.

forms.name: Complaint Log
forms.purpose: Dates received and resolved for every complaint.

forms.name: Complaint Response and Appeal Letters
forms.purpose: Written response within 15 days, appeal rights, and the governing-authority appeal review within 30 days.

forms.name: RN Intake Assessment and Acceptance Determination
forms.purpose: RN determination that the agency can safely meet the patient's needs, per written admission criteria.

forms.name: Medicaid Authorization Verification Checklist
forms.purpose: Confirms independent assessment, practitioner order, minimum-needs finding, plan authorization and Level I/II or 24-hour status.

forms.name: Plan of Care (with 6-month review)
forms.purpose: Individualized plan with services, frequency, medications, diet and limitations; documented reviews.

forms.name: Aide Task Sheet / Activity Record
forms.purpose: Aide's daily record of tasks and observations reported to the RN.

forms.name: RN Supervisory Visit Report
forms.purpose: Report of each supervisory visit, showing aide present, findings and actions; frequency per plan or contract.

forms.name: Change-in-Condition Report
forms.purpose: Aide or RN report of changes, adverse reactions and home/informal-support problems, with practitioner notification.

forms.name: Incident / Accident Report
forms.purpose: Documentation of accidents and incidents in the patient record, with QI review.

forms.name: Discharge Plan, 48-Hour Notice and Discharge Summary
forms.purpose: Discharge planning, practitioner notice, and summary elements.

forms.name: Missed Visit and Coverage Log
forms.purpose: Missed visits, reason, backup coverage and plan notification.

forms.name: EVV Exception and Reconciliation Log
forms.purpose: EVV exceptions, edits and reconciliation to authorizations before billing.

forms.name: Patient Emergency Plan
forms.purpose: Per-patient emergency contacts and continuity plan.

forms.name: Agency Emergency Plan and Employee Orientation Record
forms.purpose: Written plan and proof that all employees were oriented.

forms.name: HPN Coverage Policy and Directory Update Log
forms.purpose: 24/7 contact designations, annual review and monthly updates.

forms.name: Exposure Incident Report and Follow-up Record
forms.purpose: Reporting and follow-up of bloodborne pathogen exposures; confidential.

forms.name: Employment Application and Verification Checklist
forms.purpose: ID, employment history, references, qualifications and training source, and registry profile check.

forms.name: Criminal History Record Check Tracking Form
forms.purpose: Tracks DOH form, two fingerprint sets, 10-business-day submission, two IDs, temporary approval supervision and rejected-print resubmission.

forms.name: Employee Health Packet
forms.purpose: Health assessment, rubella and measles immunity, TB assessment/test and annual follow-up, flu vaccine or mask log; stored separately.

forms.name: Home Care Registry Entry Log
forms.purpose: Date each aide was entered or updated, start-date update within 10 business days, and designated registry users.

forms.name: Orientation and In-Service Attendance Log
forms.purpose: Hours per aide against 12/6/18-hour minimums plus Medicaid semiannual hours.

forms.name: Job Descriptions and Annual Performance Evaluation (with in-home observation)
forms.purpose: Position descriptions and the annual evaluation.

forms.name: Caregiver ID Badge Issue and Return Log
forms.purpose: Photo ID issued and returned.

forms.name: Wage Parity Certification and Audit File
forms.purpose: Annual certification and independently audited statement for downstate Medicaid work.

forms.name: QI Committee Minutes and Record Review Tool
forms.purpose: Quarterly meeting minutes, random sample of current and 3-month discharged records, complaint cases, and written summary to the governing authority.

forms.name: Management / Franchise Agreement Submission Checklist
forms.purpose: 60-day advance submission to DOH and retained-control checklist.

forms.name: Annual Reports Calendar
forms.purpose: Annual registration, statistical summary, ownership list, cost report, HERDS weekly submission.

forms.name: Record Retention and Closure Plan
forms.purpose: Retention schedule and the plan to store records and notify DOH if the agency closes.
